questions.q: Why can't Azure Cost Management data and AWS Cost Explorer data simply be added together into one total?
options: They can be added together directly; the two tools already share an identical schema
AWS does not track cost by resource at all
Azure only reports cost in a foreign currency
Each prices usage in its own format with its own separate committed-use discount model, so the raw numbers aren't in the same units until normalized
questions.explain: Azure Cost Management and AWS Cost Explorer/CUR use different meters, line-item structures, and discount models (Reservations/Savings Plans on each side), so raw totals aren't directly comparable without normalization.

questions.q: What does it mean to use 'amortized' cost rather than raw billed cost when comparing a reserved instance across providers?
options: Spreading the commitment's cost evenly across its full term instead of showing it as a lump sum in the purchase month
Ignoring reserved instances entirely in any cost report
Converting the cost into a different currency
Billing the on-prem server as if it were a cloud resource
questions.explain: Amortized cost spreads a committed-use discount evenly across its term so a reserved purchase doesn't look artificially expensive in the month it was bought and artificially cheap afterward.

questions.q: How should on-prem infrastructure cost be represented in a unified cost view, according to this lesson?
options: It should be left out of the report since there is no invoice
As an exact, invoice-grade number pulled automatically from the hardware vendor
As a fully-loaded estimate combining depreciation and operating costs, clearly labeled as an approximation
As zero cost, since the hardware was already purchased
questions.explain: On-prem cost has no bill to pull, so it's approximated with depreciation plus operating costs (power, cooling, support, staff time) and should be labeled as an estimate, not presented as exact data.

questions.q: What role does the FinOps tagging taxonomy (cost center, environment, owner, workload) play in a cross-cloud cost rollup?
options: It determines which cloud region a resource is billed in
It sets the discount tier a workload qualifies for
It acts as the shared join key that lets spend be grouped by workload across Azure and AWS in one pivot
It is only used for access control, not cost reporting
questions.explain: Consistent tag keys and values across providers are what let a report group spend by the same workload regardless of which cloud it ran on; inconsistent tags silently break the rollup.

questions.q: What is FOCUS, as described in this lesson?
options: A proprietary Azure-only billing export format
An open, vendor-neutral schema published by the FinOps Foundation for normalizing billing data across providers
A feature of AWS Cost Explorer that automatically merges in on-prem costs
A replacement for cost allocation tags
questions.explain: FOCUS (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification) is an open schema from the FinOps Foundation that normalizes billing data into a consistent set of columns across multiple providers.
